result.title: Nudging Decision Models: Do Digital Nudges Steer Fast, Generation-Free AI Agents?
result.summary: LLM-based agents increasingly automate business and consumer tasks but are slow and expensive. Decision models, a new class that chooses among options without generating text, are far faster and less costly. Developers call them "System One models," referencing dual process theory. We ask whether such models can be steered by digital nudges online and whether, as the theory predicts, automatic nudges affect them more than reflective ones. We adapted an online shopping experiment, previously run with humans and LLM agents, to three decision models (Jev, Decision-1, d1). Across 600 runs per model, they chose a preselected default in 97.5-99.9% and a product with social influence information in 75-96% of choices, versus 47-49% in the control. All responded more strongly to the automatic nudge, the opposite of what has been reported for reasoning-capable LLM agents. We provide first evidence that non-generative decision models are susceptible to digital nudges in a System 1 pattern, implying agent-type-specific nudge effects.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把在线购物的数字助推实验迁移到三个不生成文本的决策模型（Jev、Decision-1、d1），每个模型运行 600 次，比较默认选项与社会影响两类助推，发现它们对自动型助推的反应强于反思型，与具备推理能力的 LLM agent 已有报告相反。
